decisions.reason: It is very close to the firm’s existing border and passenger-security capabilities and the visible adoption by the UK Home Office and more than 30 governmental APIS schemes shows the firm can recognise, refine and commercially exploit this knowledge effectively.

This API builds on the firm’s established travel-compliance and security offer, and its continued dedicated presence in 2024 suggests enough customer relevance and internal learning potential to justify further development.

Although training is familiar to the firm, the module disappeared from the website by 2024, indicating weak traction and limited evidence that the firm’s existing knowledge was being converted into a scalable, defensible offer.

Behaviour-analysis systems are related but require stronger specialised analytical development, and the product’s disappearance by 2024 suggests the firm did not build sufficient absorptive capacity or market proof to keep investing.

Passenger security profiling is adjacent to the firm’s expertise but is demanding in terms of data, regulation and refinement, and the loss of website presence by 2024 points to insufficient commercialisation success relative to its knowledge requirements.

The web platform is close to the firm’s core document and travel-security operations, and its continued standalone presentation in 2024 indicates that the firm can leverage and extend existing know-how profitably.
